- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion or downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast growth to 3–5% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤ 0.10) and prices are trending upward, model underestimates — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% per day until sentiment reverses.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is low or flat — apply a 1–3% upward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment < 0.10.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to recognize — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days post-peak.
- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.50) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, model underestimates — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to reflect bullish sentiment.
- Avoid linear extrapolation — if history shows volatility or sentiment shifts, apply exponential decay or stepwise adjustment rather than uniform slope.
